module.purpose: Builds Pages Router-compatible request and server-side context objects from Next.js App Router headers, cookies, route parameters, and search parameters.
module.summary: This module adapts App Router request data to the legacy Pages Router context shape. It materializes read-only headers and cookies into plain objects protected by mutation-blocking proxies, decodes route parameters for backward compatibility, merges decoded route parameters with search parameters into the query, and exposes an unsupported response object that fails explicitly when accessed.
module.businessContext: Supports legacy request handlers while the application uses Next.js App Router APIs. Failures can break compatibility for pages expecting decoded parameters, legacy request fields, or explicit response behavior.
functions: createProxifiedObject (~L7-13): Protects legacy data objects from unsupported mutation attempts.
buildLegacyHeaders (~L15-19): Converts read-only request headers into a protected plain object.
buildLegacyCookies (~L21-29): Converts request cookies into a protected name-value object.
decodeParams (~L31-48): Decodes scalar and array route parameter values for compatibility.
buildLegacyRequest (~L50-52): Constructs a legacy request object from headers and cookies.
buildLegacyCtx (~L54-78): Constructs a Pages Router-compatible server-side context object.

invariants.description: Headers and cookies returned through legacy adapters cannot be modified successfully.
Decoded parameter output preserves parameter keys and array structure.
Context query merges search parameters before decoded route parameters.
Context route parameters are always passed through parameter decoding.
The context response object is intentionally unsupported and rejects property access.

assumptions.description: Callers provide Next.js read-only headers and cookies objects implementing the methods used here.
Parameter values are strings, string arrays, or undefined as represented by Params.
Callers expecting a response object do not access its properties in App Router mode.

ambiguities.question: Should duplicate cookie names preserve the first value or the last value?
Is the unsupported response proxy intended to reject only reads, or should other proxy operations also be blocked?

concurrencyModel.notes: All transformations are synchronous and operate on newly created objects; no shared mutable state or asynchronous work is used.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A params object contains a percent-encoded scalar value.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Preserves Pages Router-compatible decoding for scalar route parameters.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A params object contains an array of percent-encoded values.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ensures every array element is decoded independently.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A params object contains an undefined value.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Undefined optional route parameters must remain absent in value.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Readonly headers and cookies are provided to the request adapter.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the legacy request shape and conversion of framework collections to objects.

moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins query merging, decoded route params, and legacy context compatibility.

moduleContractTests.then: throws Error("You are trying to access the 'res' property of the context, which is not supported in app dir")
